title: Protocol for generation of multicellular spheroids through reduced gravity
protocol: Remove culture media from cells in cell culture plates.
Wash each plate with 7 mL of PBS and remove.
Add 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin/EDTA to each plate.
Incubate at 37°C for 3–5 min, until fully detached.
Add 8 mL of complete media to each plate to neutralize trypsin.
Collect cell suspensions in individual 15 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge cell suspensions for 5 min at 300 × g and 4°C.
Remove and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellets in 2 mL of respective complete media by gently pipetting up and down.
Combine 10 μL of resuspended cell solution with 10 μL of trypan blue for a total of 20 μL.
Pipette 10 μL of the solution onto a cell counting chamber slide.
Count cells using an automated cell counter.
Combine HH with LX2 cells in individual 1.5 mL tubes with a volume of 500–600 μL.
Combine cancer cells with LX2 cells in individual 1.5 mL tubes with a volume of 500–600 μL.
Centrifuge cell suspensions in the 1.5 mL tubes for 5 min at 300 × g at 4°C.
Remove and discard media without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in 60 μL of mixed media from step 12 and transfer to 0.2 mL microfuge tube.
Place tubes onto clinostat in a 37°C incubator.
Set the clinostat to 18 RPM.
Allow the clinostat to run for 90 minutes.
Remove tubes from the clinostat.
Add 100 μL of spheroids specific mixed media to the tubes.
Vortex tubes for 5 seconds.
Ensure that cells remain well suspended after vortexing.
Fill tubes completely with mixed media and return to the clinostat.
Set clinostat to 18 RPM and allow it to run for 15–18 hours.
Remove tubes from the clinostat.
Cut the top of 200 μL pipette tips using sterilized scissors.
Transfer spheroids into 1.5 mL tubes filled completely with appropriate media.
Return tubes to the clinostat at 18 RPM and allow it to run for 24 hours.
Remove tubes from the clinostat.
Place samples in a tube holder in the sterile cell culture hood.
Allow spheroids to settle by gravity to the bottom of the tube for 20-40 seconds.
Carefully remove 1.3 mL of media from the tube.
Replace the removed volume with fresh complete media.
Manually ensure that spheroids are suspended through rotation of the tube.
Place tubes back into the tube holder and set the clinostat to 18 RPM.
Allow the clinostat to run for 24 hours.
Remove tubes from the clinostat and bring them to a bright field microscope.
Image spheroids at any desired time during the 72-hour period to ensure development is proceeding as expected.
Position the tube over the objective and acquire desired images.
Remove tubes from the clinostat.
Place samples in a tube holder in the sterile cell culture hood.
Allow spheroids to settle by gravity for 20-40 seconds.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Replace with 500 μL of PBS.
Transfer spheroids into one chamber of a four-chamber microscope slide using a cut 1,000 μL pipette tip.
Image spheroids using a bright field microscope.
Transfer and divide spheroids from the chamber slide evenly into two 1.5 mL tubes using a cut pipette tip.
Allow spheroids to settle in one of the 1.5 mL tubes.
Remove PBS.
Incubate spheroids in 300 μL of calcein-AM/propidium iodide solution for 4 min.
Image spheroids via bright field microscopy and fluorescence microscopy promptly after 4-minute incubation time.
Allow the spheroids in the second 1.5 mL tube to settle to the bottom.
Remove PBS from the tube.
Add 300 μL of 10% formalin to the tube and incubate at 20°C–22°C for at least 24 h.
Carefully remove and properly discard 10% formalin after spheroids have settled.
Wash with 500 μL of PBS.
Allow spheroids to fully settle and remove PBS.
Add 50 μL of warmed HistoGel to the tube.
Using a cut pipette tip, transfer HistoGel containing spheroids to a disposable histology mold and place spheroids in a small bead.
Let the mixture slightly solidify at 20°C–22°C for 1–2 min.
Fill the rest of the mold with warm HistoGel and place on ice for 5 min.
Remove solidified HistoGel from the mold and place it in a tissue cassette.
Keep the tissue cassette in 70% Ethanol.
Perform sample paraffinization, deparaffinization, and rehydration as per standard in-house protocol.
Retrieve antigen using target retrieval solution, citrate pH 6.1 (Agilent, #S169984-2) for 25 min at 100°C.
Allow slides to cool in the solution at 20°C–22°C for 25 min.
Rinse slides with water 2–3 times and place them in TBST.
Block endogenous peroxides with 0.3% hydrogen peroxide (Abcam, #ab64218) for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse slides with TBST.
Incubate slides in serum free protein block (Agilent, #X0909) for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Proceed with immunohistochemical staining for cell type verification.
Incubate slide with 300 μL of primary antibody for 60 min at 20°C–22°C.
After incubation, rinse the slide with TBST.
Incubate slide with 300 μL of predilute Envision Plus anti-rabbit labeled polymer for 30 min at 20°C–22°C, rinse slides with TBST.
Incubate slides with 300 μL of predilute DAB+ for 5 min at 20°C–22°C, rinse with distilled water.
Counter stain slide with 300 μL of predilute Gills I hematoxylin for 30 s, rinse with water.
Dehydrate slides.
Clear slides.
Mount slides.
Open the ImageJ Fiji application.
Access the folder containing spheroid images.
Drag and drop the image into ImageJ Fiji.
Select the line tool from the toolbar.
Measure the image scale bar by left clicking and holding to trace its length.
Select the analyze tab from the menu options.
Set the scale from the drop-down menu.
Edit the “known distance” and “unit length” options to match the distance and unit in the selected image.
Select the “global” box and click “ok”.
Select the line tool from the menu options.
Draw a line across the longest diameter of the spheroid then click “M” on the keyboard to save the measurement.
Draw a line across the smallest diameter of the same spheroid and click “M”.
Copy data from ImageJ Fiji into an excel spreadsheet.
Format data so that the length and width of each spheroid in the dataset are identifiable.
Apply the formula volume = π d³ / 6, where d is equal to the average of the length and width of the spheroids, to estimate spheroid volumes.
